endorsements.quote: Tools should be codesigned alongside a range of relevant clinicians and members of the public to ensure they address a strategic clinical need and align with policy priorities.
Tools must be able to demonstrate clinical effectiveness in real-world contexts and document workflow impact and unintended consequences.
HCPs should receive training and education before implementation to facilitate routine use and alleviate negative perceptions.
Tools should strive to be integrated with EHR and incumbent technology.
Tools must demonstrate compliance with legal, regulatory and data protection frameworks to facilitate trust and confidence, for example, MHRA guidance on regulating medical devices.
Algorithms should demonstrate sufficient predictive performance and undergo validity testing ahead of implementation.
There should be ongoing access to technical support for users and opportunity for users to provide feedback.

unlisted_practices: Developers should be transparent about the impact of missing or poor-quality input data on the uncertainty and accuracy of a tool's outputs.
Developers should report the development and validation of risk prediction models transparently in line with established guidelines such as TRIPOD+AI.
Monitor, maintain and update risk prediction tools over time to track automation bias, mitigate distributional shift and ensure ongoing clinical effectiveness.
Design tools for intuitive integration with clinical workflows to avoid disrupting the physician/patient relationship.
Co-design patient-facing outputs with the public and clinicians so they are patient-oriented and accessible, in line with established guidelines such as Double Diamond and WCAG.
Make tools interoperable using standardised taxonomy.
Incorporate efficient algorithms and shared compute resources to minimise the environmental burden of risk tools.

screen.reason: This is a consensus-based recommendations paper combining an umbrella review and stakeholder workshops to generate guidance for the design and implementation of predictive risk AI tools in primary care.
